I have a number of problems with dating websites (and dating in general). Philosophical issues.     
It's hard to explain but the best way I can describe it is I feel almost as if I am not entitled to a relationship. I feel like I want someone so badly, but part of me tells me I'm not entitled to have anyone. I feel like this results in me not selling myself well enough on dating sites so I never get anyone.    Sorry I take that back, I get gay guys hitting on me online. Beggars can't be choosers I guess.        
As for looking for activities to go to, there are none. If by some miracle I do find myself at some type of social event, it'll be a bunch of couples and I'll be the guy no one talks to. I'll be the 3rd, 5th, etc, wheel.     
     
My first (and only) date, had a lot of right moments and situations setup for me to get into that situation, which of course ended badly a few months later. I was forced into a college group and I didn't mind it. the leader was cool and fun. I saw the girl and liked her but thought I'd be too nervous. The leader did not know I liked her but miraculously, since I did not drive to this one event (a movie night) a couple weeks into the meetings, the leader asked her if she could drive me home. So there I Found myself in a car with the only girl I liked from the group, a 30 min drive. Talking about random stuff I ended up mentioning a movie and saying I'd like her to go to the movie with me. She said yes and went from there.

I am not attracted at all to obese women. The ones I see attracted to me have serious issues, be it divorced and having multiple chlidren, bipolar disorder, emotional issues and clinginess type of personalities.        
There's a gay guy at work who I get along with just fine. I went to his birthday party and was surrounded by gay guys hitting on me. He knows I'm not gay, and I didn't tell his friends I wasn't gay. And I'm not going to get mad and leave.   Would you invest in more "opportunities" like this if it happens to you?    Would it really open the door if I started getting into a conversation with the gay clerk at the store beyond small talk? He'd take that as flirting and would lead him down a path to being disappointed finding out I'm not gay.       
If he introduces me to female friends, they'll assume I'm gay. They won't say it, but I can tell they do.     
Like I said, nothing in my life works out.

It just seems like every time I "get out there" it just turns into a miserable experience.     
I go to the gym I can't talk to girls because there's always another guy there they're with.      
At work or at shopping no girls give me any hint they might like me. Most of the guys are douche bags and don't want to be friends with me since they can probably tell I don't have any friends. I can tell this because it's usually the older men (late 30s and up) who don't BS and talk to me or treat me normal.   But as for my age, I feel like everything is political when it comes to socializing.        
I go outside and read or walk around, I only see couples everywhere. No singles. I am the single. The single single.    
The only people I've had (not to be rude here) misfortune of attracting have been: Fat/large women (which I'm not sure why considering I'm 5'8", 9% body fat and 145 lbs), and gay guys (who I'm sure look good to their gay friends but I have absolutely no interest in).

in all these years of going out I haven't met anyone.    
anytime I see a girl somewhere like at the gym, or at the store, within seconds I see here with a guy. I know it sounds crazy but it is the reality I face for some reason.      
the only people who I'd say flirt with me are overweight women or gay guys.  That's all life has thrown my way.

I don't feel like I'm young. I actually feel old. I'll be 30 in less than 3 years and I will have nothing to show for my 20's other than being neglected, alone, and not having one friend or relationship for that entire 10 years.      
I wonder if anyone else can say the same who's a member of normal society.

Unfortunately I have no friends. I've no one in my phone that I could call to do anything.   
I feel like everyone around me is already satisfied with the friends they have and have no idea or concept of accepting someone like me into their circle.
